summary.summary: Somerset's year-end treasury report shows borrowing of £716m against a £990m ceiling, with everything compliant — but 39.4% of the debt falls due within twelve months, close to the council's own 50% limit, so a large slice must be refinanced at whatever rates arrive. Housing-account financing costs took 11% of housing income this year and the council's own projections take that to 18.3% by 2030/31. The legacy commercial property portfolio (bought for £301m, written down heavily) is being sold off: £33.3m of sales this year at a £4.7m net gain, £82.3m still to go.

compliance.notes: Strong core treasury strategy: an exemplary Arlingclose-style liability benchmark (charted to 2075 and actively used), thorough counterparty/creditworthiness framework, full indicator suite over six years, and a completed exit review of legacy commercial investments. The weak flank is the commercial/non-treasury disclosure set within the supplied papers - no commercial-income-to-revenue ratio (PI-08), no proportionality demonstration (COM-03) and no service/commercial investment limits (COM-09); much of this should live in the separate Non-Treasury Investment Strategy (Appendix T/E), which was not among the supplied PDFs, and the sterling-only borrowing statement (BOR-03) and specified/non-specified categories (INV-05) are also missing from the TMS itself.

news_drafts.headline: Somerset audit of 2025-26 accounts "in a healthy position", with November sign-off planned
news_drafts.lead:
Somerset Council's audit of its 2025-26 accounts is "in a healthy position", according to its external auditor, the accountancy firm Grant Thornton. A progress report went to the Audit Committee on 28 September. The external audit is an independent check on the council's accounts. Sign-off is planned for November.

The national deadline for completing the audit is 31 January 2027. The council's own report says there remains a risk that it will not meet that date. It scores that risk at 4, calculated as likelihood multiplied by impact, against a target score of 2. Grant Thornton says keeping up momentum in October is important to support the November sign-off.

The report sets out what a missed deadline would mean. It says it could result in "a further modified audit opinion or audit assurance limitations", and could affect the council's future approach to rebuilding audit assurance. The papers describe the consequence as financial and reputational risk. The report uses the word "further", which indicates the council's accounts have previously received a modified opinion. The papers provided do not say for which year.
news_drafts.paper_title: External Audit Progress for the 2025-26 Accounts - September 26 - Cover Report

findings.headline: Funds Held on Behalf of Others is shown at £5.226m at 1 April 2026 and £1.755m at closing, with no adjustment, in-year or other movement entered.
findings.detail: The Other Earmarked Reserves table shows the balance falling by £3.471m, but the movement columns are blank for this row. The Appendix does not explain the change. The Revenue Grants and Schools Reserves rows also show closing balances that differ from opening balances after the movements shown.
findings.matters: A balance that falls without a recorded movement is a reconciliation point an auditor or finance director would check before accepting the closing figure.
findings.quote: Funds Held on Behalf of Others 5.226 - - - 1.755

findings.headline: An initial review releases four service reserves into the Business Risk Reserve, including £0.600m of historic Building Control support service costs.
findings.detail: The Reserves Review lists Ash Die Back (£0.170m), Building Control Rolling Reserve (£0.600m), Minehead Shelters (£0.017m) and Sustainable Drainage Funding (£0.015m). The Building Control amount is an historic support service cost adjustment for charges not made in prior years. The Appendix says the wider review is ongoing and will be updated at budget setting.
findings.matters: Service reserves being reviewed and released into a corporate risk reserve is a common step, and the historic Building Control adjustment shows a trading account being brought up to full cost.
findings.figures: £0.170m Ash Die Back; £0.600m Building Control; £0.017m Minehead Shelters; £0.015m Sustainable Drainage Funding
findings.quote: An initial review of reserves has taken place with amount detailed in the table above being released

findings.headline: The Corporate Risk budget of £2.000m has been moved into reserve to be drawn as required.
findings.detail: The Appendix shows a £2.000m in-year contribution to the Corporate Risk reserve, and a corporate reserves adjustment of £2.679m in the MTFP and carry-forward table. Corporate Reserves are forecast to close at £26.103m.
findings.matters: Holding a corporate risk budget in reserve rather than in revenue is a choice a finance director would compare against their own risk provision.
findings.figures: £2.000m contribution; £2.679m corporate adjustment; £26.103m corporate reserves closing balance
findings.quote: The Corporate Risk budget has been moved to reserve and

findings.headline: A £1.777m unallocated contingency is moved to a reserve for costs relating to a recent fire at Saxonvale.
findings.detail: The Appendix states that the remaining unallocated contingency has been moved to a reserve to fund costs from the recent fire. No further detail on the fire or expected costs is given in this paper.
findings.matters: A council setting aside contingency for a specific incident is useful to peers planning how to handle unbudgeted costs from property damage.
findings.quote: in order to fund any costs relating to the recent fire.

findings.headline: The S151 Officer has recommended two reserve contributions totalling £3.777m, which are shown as pending agreement.
findings.detail: The Appendix lists a £2.000m contribution for the Corporate Risk budget and a £1.777m contribution from unallocated contingency to a Saxonvale Site Recovery reserve for costs relating to a recent fire. Both are shown as recommended, not yet approved.
findings.matters: Moving unspent budget into reserves to cover a specific incident is a decision other councils face after an unplanned event, and the approval step matters for how the balance is reported.
